title: mnrfit
summary: Fit nominal multinomial logistic regression coefficients.

gpu_support.notes: The multinomial logistic solver runs on CPU. Automatic internal residency gathers transparently; explicit gpuArray input is a mode-gated RunMat host-fallback extension.

description: `mnrfit(X,Y)` fits nominal multinomial logistic regression coefficients for predictor matrix `X` and response `Y`. Rows of `X` are observations, columns are predictors, and columns of `B` correspond to all response classes except the final sorted reference class.
behaviors: `X` must be a finite real numeric matrix with observations in rows and predictors in columns.
Current MATLAB documents single or double X. Typed-integer X, typed-integer Y, and logical X are independently gated RunMat extensions; logical Y remains documented.
Admitted integer predictor, response, weight, and tolerance values must be exactly representable at the binary64 host-solver boundary.
`Y` may be a numeric, logical, string, character, cellstr, or categorical class vector with one response per row of `X`. Classes are sorted, and the final class is used as the reference category.
`Y` may also be an `N`-by-K numeric grouped-counts matrix. Columns are treated as response categories, and row totals become multinomial observation weights.
`B = mnrfit(...)` returns a coefficient matrix with one row per model term and one column per non-reference class. A constant term is included by default.
`[B,dev,stats] = mnrfit(...)` returns model deviance and a stats structure containing `beta`, `se`, `t`, `p`, `covb`, `coeffcorr`, `dfe`, `s`, `estdisp`, and `classNames`.
`Weights` accepts a nonnegative finite observation-weight vector with positive total weight. `IterationLimit` and `Tolerance` control Newton solver convergence.
`Constant`, `MaxIter`, `TolX`, `Options`, and `Display` are retained as explicitly gated RunMat option extensions rather than being presented as current MATLAB-compatible spellings.
Rows with `NaN` in `X`, numeric `Y`, or grouped counts are omitted before fitting.
`Display` is accepted for compatibility. Overdispersion estimation is not implemented, so `EstDisp` must be `"off"`.

examples.description: Fit a binary nominal logistic model
examples.output: B has two rows, one intercept and one predictor coefficient. stats.se has the same shape as B.
B has two columns because the final sorted class is the reference category.
Y columns contribute grouped response counts, and B has one column per non-reference category.
stats.classNames is returned as a string array containing the sorted response classes.

faqs.question: Which response class is the reference class?
faqs.answer: RunMat sorts numeric or logical response classes and uses the final sorted class as the reference, matching the default nominal coding used by MATLAB-style multinomial fits.

faqs.question: Does RunMat implement ordinal models?
faqs.answer: No. The current implementation is for nominal multinomial logistic regression. `Model` values other than `"nominal"` return a compatibility error.

faqs.question: Does RunMat estimate overdispersion?
faqs.answer: No. `EstDisp` is accepted only as `"off"`; stats.s is returned as 1.
